title: Remediation Portfolio SLA Foundation
goal: Extend first-slice remediation into portfolio-level closure visibility without replacing the existing finding workflow.
scope: Add a first portfolio remediation queue with SLA visibility, ownership filters, and batch retest planning based on existing remediation records and linked retest runs. Keep actual retest dispatch approval-aware and explicit.
generation_reason: Product recommendation coverage audit found SLA tracking and batch remediation follow-up were not explicit after the first remediation slice.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Build portfolio visibility and planning only. Do not add automatic retest dispatch, SLA enforcement, or ticketing worker automation.
notes: Batch retests must remain explicit and approval-aware.
SLA status must be transparent and configurable, not hard-coded as contractual truth.

success_criteria: Operators can review remediation items across findings or runs with owner and SLA context.
Batch retest planning can group eligible findings without automatically dispatching scans.
Overdue, due-soon, verified, and blocked states are distinguishable.
Browser/API tests cover portfolio review and approval-aware retest planning.
Existing single-finding remediation flow remains intact.
must_not_touch: pack registry, validation, approval, deployment, or runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: Portfolio remediation view uses existing remediation records.
Batch retest planning does not bypass approval.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
Existing remediation record and retest linkage behavior is inspected.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with remediation portfolio changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the remediation portfolio baseline and remaining automation limits.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
